\[
I_{\text{out}}(x, y) = I(x, y) - I(x - 1, y + 1) + 128
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I(x, y)\): The input at column x and row y, with y growing downward

This is Pillow's EMBOSS filter. Pillow lists its kernel with -1 at the top left and 1 in the center, but applies the first row of a kernel to the row below the pixel. So the -1 falls on the pixel below and to the left, as a single bright pixel shows. y grows downward. Flat areas turn mid gray, 128. Where the image gets brighter toward the top right, the result is lighter, and where it gets darker, the result is darker.
